name: release-notes
title: Release Notes
description: Every Beacon release as one post, newest first: two or three features with captioned screenshots, then the release’s full Added / Changed / Fixed changelog in the Claude Code layout. Real customer-facing 1.39–1.41 notes; the help bar’s What’s-new popover lists the latest post’s features.

guide.intent: A slim sticky list of release versions on the end side of the page, each an anchor link to its post. A scroll-spy mirrors whichever release is in view into an active highlight. Wide screens only.
decisions: PROGRESSIVE BY CONSTRUCTION: the rows are plain in-page anchor links that jump to each release with no JS. The IntersectionObserver only mirrors the in-view release into an active class.
Versions only. Each post carries its own version badge and date in its meta column, so the rail repeats neither the date nor a "Latest" marker.
The active state is an ink shift, never a color fill: the version darkens and gains weight.
Below 64rem the rail is not rendered; the posts' own meta columns carry the version.
gotchas: The rail sticks INSIDE the .modern-layout__content scroll container, which already begins below the fixed topbar. Its sticky `top` is a small breathing gap, not the topbar height.
The PAGE owns the .sidebar primitive (data-side="end", --sidebar-width 12rem); the rail is its first-child aside.
acceptance: Every release has a row; clicking one jumps to that post with landing room below the topbar; scrolling moves the active ink down the rail; the rail is absent on a phone.

sections.label: Release post
sections.html:
1.41.0

October 13, 2026

Lists replace Action Lists

Each project now has one Lists page for action lists and commitment lists. Every list has its own page, with a searchable drawer for adding items, Select mode for removing many, and CSV export.

The Action Lists entry in the navigation is gone on every tenant. Your lists are all on the new page.

Configurable Monitoring Portal dashboard

The dashboard is now a board of widgets. Admins add them from a gallery, then resize, reorder, recolor and configure each one, and the layout is saved for the project.

Monitoring pages moved under each project’s new Data page. Old links redirect.

Evidence for a whole action list

Choose a component, stage the evidence, and save it to every action on that component in one step.

Added

  • Added a Lists page to every project that holds action lists and commitment lists together, with keyword search and an Add button for each kind of list
  • Added a page for every list, with editable details, sharing and delete, and views by type, by commitment or A to Z

Changed

  • Changed Action Lists to Lists: the Action Lists entry in the navigation is gone on every tenant
  • Changed where evidence is associated: one dialog on the evidence record’s page replaces Associate To Actions and the Associated Work Areas picker

Fixed

  • Fixed deleting a component; the dialog now asks for the component’s name and shows what is removed and what is kept
  • Fixed the Components link showing in a project’s navigation when Components are turned off

guide.intent: One release, as one post: the version badge and date in a narrow meta column, then two or three features (title, paragraph, optional note on what moved (info icon + text), screenshot in an inset frame with a caption), then the release's full Added / Changed / Fixed list. Every release uses the same shape.
decisions: Features first, changelog second: a reader who stops after the features knows what matters; the changelog is the complete record beneath.

The meta column is the Claude Code changelog layout (160px column, 24px gap). It sticks while its post scrolls once the two sit side by side; on a phone it drops above the body as one row (badge, date).
Version is an esa-badge (neutral, lg), not a brand-tinted pill: badges stay quiet per the design principles.
A serif display layer (--font-decorative) carries the feature titles; everything else is the sans body face. No status color anywhere.
Headlines are plain and factual: they name the feature, not a pitch. There is no per-release summary line; the features lead.

Screenshots sit in an inset frame: a sunken panel with padding and a large radius around an image with its own smaller radius and a hairline, and a short factual caption under it. The caption is the alt text too.

A feature note is the info icon and the fact itself ("The Action Lists entry in the navigation is gone on every tenant."), with no "Read this first" label: the label addressed the reader instead of stating the change.
Every post is a hash target (#v1-41-0) and every feature is too (#v1-41-0-lists), with scroll-margin for landing room.
gotchas: Each post is the .sidebar layout primitive. Sticky needs the meta column to stretch (align-self: stretch) and the inner wrapper to stick; sticking the wrapped phone layout would float the badge over the body, so sticky is media-gated.
Feature screenshots come from one prop (feature.image). Where production captures come from is still open; swap the source, not the layout.
acceptance: Each release shows badge and date, two or three features each with a captioned, inset screenshot, then Added / Changed / Fixed; a feature note renders only where the data has one; the meta column sticks on desktop and sits above the body on a phone.

guide.intent: The release's complete list of changes, grouped Added, Changed, Fixed, in a dense 14px bulleted list below a hairline.
decisions: Lines that belong to one product area lead with that area as a quiet esa-badge (sm). App-wide lines carry no badge.
A value as it appears in Beacon (a status or outcome name, written in backticks in the data) renders bold, not monospace: monospace is reserved for code.
Group heads are 14px semibold labels in normal case, never ornamental micro-labels.
gotchas: Every line starts with its group's verb (Added, Changed, Fixed) so a line read alone still says what happened.
Customer Announcements only: ESA Internal, Dev-only, TBD items and Jira keys stay out of the data.
acceptance: Each release shows its three groups in order; area badges align with the first line of text; backticked values read bold.

All release notes

guide.intent: The app-wide entry point to this page: a popover above the floating help bar with the latest release's version pill and date, its features, one row per earlier release, and an "All release notes" footer.
decisions: Derived, not curated separately: the entries are LATEST_RELEASE.features, so the popover and the post always agree.
Each entry is the feature title (serif) over its one-sentence `summary`, written for the popover. No clamping or ellipsis; the page has the full paragraph.
Each entry links to `<release-notes>#<release anchor>-<feature id>`, landing on the feature itself.

Under "Earlier", the two releases before the latest get one row each: a smaller version pill and that release's feature titles joined by " · ", linking to the release's anchor. No dates on these rows.
No screenshots and no unread dot: the button is a doorway, not a notifier.
The panel is the esa-popover lego (position="top", trigger="click"), which owns open/close, Esc and outside-click. The bar's own script only fits the panel to narrow screens.
gotchas: Trigger the popover from the real button.
esa-popover exposes no public padding or radius hook, so the bar sets its private --_popover-padding, --_popover-radius and --_popover-bg.
acceptance: Clicking What's new opens a white panel above the bar headed by the latest version pill and date; it lists that release's features with a one-sentence summary each; clicking one lands on that feature on this page; each Earlier row lands on that release.

sections.label: Guidance drawer — curated route context
sections.html:
Release Notes

What changed in each Beacon release — the main features with screenshots, then everything added, changed and fixed, newest first.

On this page

Terms

guide.intent: Aldo's opening message on THIS route — the route-aware half of the guidance drawer. "You are here" names the page and states its purpose in plain words; "On this page" lists the how-to articles curated for it; "Terms" lists the glossary terms it uses. Every page gets this; the Release Notes route has a curated entry rather than the generic fallback.
decisions: Route context is a DATA RECORD, not logic: HELP_ROUTE_CONTEXTS is an ordered list of { pattern, page, purpose, howtos, terms }, matched by pathname substring with FIRST MATCH WINNING. Adding guidance for a route is a data edit.
HELP_GENERAL_CONTEXT is the fallback for any route without a curated entry, so the drawer is never empty — an uncurated page still gets an orienting answer.
The pattern is a base-agnostic pathname substring, so the same record works under the prototype base path and in the real app.

howtos and terms are ARRAYS OF ARTICLE IDS into the one shared dataset — the drawer never holds its own copy of an article. Curating a route means choosing which existing articles surface, not writing new text.
The Release Notes entry curates to what this page actually raises: the how-to for tenant settings and the "feature flag" glossary term — matching the flag notes on the entries above.
Section labels are readable words with a leading esa-icon glyph (map-pin / list / book), not ornamental micro-labels.

Rendering is a MOVE, not a build: every article is pre-rendered once as a row into a hidden pool, and the client moves the matched route's rows into these two sections. Astro is compile-time and the drawer is route-agnostic at build, so the move is what makes it route-aware.
gotchas: Order matters in HELP_ROUTE_CONTEXTS — first match wins, so a broad pattern placed above a specific one will shadow it. Keep specific routes before general ones.
A curated entry whose howtos or terms name an id that no longer exists silently renders one fewer row. Validate the ids against the dataset at build time.
The "On this page" and "Terms" sections hide themselves when their list is empty — a curated entry with no terms should not leave a labeled empty section.
This intro is a message in the chat stream, not a fixed header: it scrolls away as the conversation grows. Do not pin it.
acceptance: Opening the drawer on this route shows "Release Notes" with its purpose sentence, the curated how-to row, and the "feature flag" term; opening it on an uncurated route shows the general fallback instead of an empty drawer; every listed row opens that article in the stacked reader.
